- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast slope or add early mean-reversion bias.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and forecast is below recent history mean, model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcomes in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% upward bias for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 0.80 to 0.00), model often fails to anticipate sharp drop; add 2–5% downward buffer in forecast if sentiment drops below 0.27.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5% from recent peak), forecast should be adjusted to reflect 1–2 day lag in correction.
